name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
meta_description: Investigative consulting for matters touching Saint Kitts and Nevis: Nevis entity research, citizenship by investment background checks and ECSC litigation support.
eyebrow: Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Saint Kitts and Nevis usually concerns entities formed on Nevis, individuals holding citizenship by investment and disputes before the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court. Work centres on lawful records research, ownership analysis and background verification, with any local step coordinated through qualified professionals and counsel.
intro: Saint Kitts and Nevis is a two-island federation with a common law legal system, the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court as its superior court and the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council as its final court of appeal. Company law differs between the islands: companies in Saint Kitts are formed under the Companies Act, while Nevis has its own corporate legislation, including the Nevis Island Business Corporation Ordinance, and a long-established international financial services sector. Registration involves the Financial Services Regulatory Commission and the Registrar of Companies. For investigators, the federation's structure means confirming at the outset which island and which statute govern an entity, and recognising that public access to ownership information is limited.

Organisations commission investigative work involving Saint Kitts and Nevis for two main reasons. First, Nevis companies, limited liability companies and trusts appear in international ownership structures, so litigants, lenders and compliance teams need to understand who stands behind them. Second, the federation operates one of the longest-running citizenship by investment programmes, and employers, banks, counterparties and courts sometimes need to understand the background of individuals holding second citizenship. Other exposures arise in tourism and real estate development, the ship registry and international education. Typical matters include asset tracing in fraud and insolvency cases, enhanced due diligence on investors and verification of claimed business histories.
legal_system: Saint Kitts and Nevis has a common law legal system derived from English law. The Supreme Court of Judicature, established under the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court arrangements shared with other OECS states, comprises the High Court and the Eastern Caribbean Court of Appeal; final appeals lie to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London. The Caribbean Court of Justice has original jurisdiction on CARICOM treaty matters but no appellate jurisdiction. Arbitration is governed by the Arbitration Act (Cap. 3.01), and the Court of Appeal also offers mediation.

data_protection.summary: Saint Kitts and Nevis adopted a Data Protection Act in 2018 to protect personal data processed by public and private bodies. As of 2024, the US State Department reported no measures restricting companies from transmitting customer data outside the country, so localisation is not a general requirement. Investigations that collect personal information about individuals in the federation should nonetheless follow the Act's principles of lawful and limited processing, protect the data securely and document the purpose. Constitutional protections and the common law of confidence also apply. Because guidance on the Act's application is limited, TDSC confirms data handling with local counsel where personal data will be collected in the federation.

investigator_regulation: We have not identified, from official sources available to us, a dedicated licensing regime for private investigators in Saint Kitts and Nevis. The legal position of private investigative activity, including surveillance, recording and approaches to witnesses, should be confirmed with local counsel before any step is taken locally. In a small jurisdiction, discretion is essential and inquiries can quickly become known. TDSC therefore relies principally on documentary and open-source research conducted from Nashville and, where local work is required, coordinates appropriately qualified professionals within limits agreed with counsel.
corporate_records: Companies in Saint Kitts are incorporated under the Companies Act and companies in Nevis under the Nevis Island Business Corporation Ordinance, with other Nevis legislation governing limited liability companies and trusts. All registered companies must maintain a local registered office. Public registries generally confirm an entity's existence, registration date and registered agent, but shareholder and beneficial ownership information held by registered agents and regulators is not generally available to the public. Court judgments of the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court are published. Ownership questions are therefore usually answered through litigation records, foreign filings, court disclosure orders and other lawful sources.
anti_corruption: The Integrity in Public Life Act, as amended, sets a code of conduct and declarations of interest for public officials, and a 2023 anti-corruption bill provided for criminal penalties for official corruption and a special prosecutor's office. Anti-money laundering legislation was updated in 2019, together with proceeds of crime and asset recovery legislation, and virtual asset businesses are regulated under 2020 legislation as amended in 2021. The Royal Saint Kitts and Nevis Police Force, the Director of Public Prosecutions and the Financial Intelligence Unit are the principal enforcement bodies.

matters.title: Nevis entity ownership research
matters.text: Identifying the people and assets behind Nevis corporations, LLCs and trusts that appear in fraud, insolvency, divorce or commercial disputes, using registry confirmations, litigation in the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court and other courts, foreign filings and media, and supporting counsel seeking disclosure orders.

matters.title: Economic citizen background checks
matters.text: Enhanced due diligence on individuals who hold Saint Kitts and Nevis citizenship by investment alongside other nationalities, examining identity history, prior names, business record, litigation, sanctions exposure and media in the jurisdictions where they actually live and work.

matters.title: Asset tracing in fraud matters
matters.text: Supporting victims and insolvency practitioners pursuing assets routed through federation entities, combining corporate genealogy, transaction analysis from client records, real estate research and coordination with Eastern Caribbean counsel on freezing and disclosure applications.

matters.title: Real estate and project counterparties
matters.text: Background research on developers, sponsors and contractors in tourism and real estate projects, including those approved for investment programmes, covering corporate history, prior projects, litigation and financial difficulties, for lenders, purchasers and partners.

matters.title: Ship registry and maritime diligence
matters.text: Research on owners and managers of vessels flagged or previously flagged in the federation's ship registry, including ownership changes, related companies and adverse media, to support charterers, insurers and compliance teams evaluating maritime counterparties.

tdsc_approach: TDSC scopes engagements touching Saint Kitts and Nevis from Nashville and begins by establishing which island's legislation governs each entity, since Saint Kitts and Nevis maintain separate corporate regimes. Research relies on registry confirmations, published Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court and Privy Council judgments, foreign corporate and court filings, property and maritime records and media. Because ownership information is generally held by registered agents rather than publicly, TDSC works with counsel where a disclosure order or other court process is the lawful route to it. Any local inquiry is discreet, agreed with counsel and carried out by appropriately qualified professionals. Personal data is handled consistently with the Data Protection Act 2018 and minimised throughout. TDSC does not provide legal advice.

faqs.q: Can you find out who owns a Nevis LLC?
faqs.a: Not usually from public registries alone, which confirm existence and the registered agent but rarely ownership. We build a picture from litigation, foreign filings, transaction records available to the client, property and media sources. Where a definitive answer is needed, counsel may seek a disclosure order from the court, and we support that application with evidence.

faqs.q: What can be verified about someone with Saint Kitts and Nevis citizenship by investment?
faqs.a: Government programme files are not public and we do not seek access to them. We research the person's identity history, business activity, litigation, sanctions exposure and media coverage, mainly in the countries where they live and operate. Second citizenship is lawful; the purpose is to understand the full background of the individual.

faqs.q: Which court hears commercial disputes in the federation?
faqs.a: The High Court of the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court hears commercial disputes at first instance, with appeals to the Eastern Caribbean Court of Appeal and, finally, the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council. Many judgments are published, which makes court records a useful source for background and ownership research.

faqs.q: Does Saint Kitts and Nevis restrict sending personal data abroad?
faqs.a: As of 2024, the US State Department reported no measures restricting companies from transmitting customer data outside the country. The Data Protection Act 2018 still governs how personal data is processed, so TDSC limits collection to what the matter requires and confirms handling with local counsel where data is gathered locally.

faqs.q: Will TDSC send investigators to Saint Kitts or Nevis?
faqs.a: Only where a local step is genuinely needed and lawful. We have not identified a dedicated investigator licensing regime, and in a small community inquiries are quickly noticed. Most questions can be answered through records and open sources. Where they cannot, local work is planned with counsel and carried out by qualified professionals.
